data.title: Anthropic shares extend gains, recovering from post-IPO slump
data.description:
Anthropic (ANT) shares surged roughly 9% at $90.06 on Friday, recovering from a rocky start to life as a publicly traded company.

The stock had snapped a three-session losing streak on Wednesday, ending 1.08% higher ahead of the Thanksgiving break but remained below IPO price. 

Three consecutive sessions of losses had pushed shares to $81.9, below their $83 IPO price, wiping out the gains from its much-anticipated Nasdaq debut.

In its Nasdaq debut on Nov. 19, the stock opened at $111.50 and hit an intraday high of $115.10.

Anthropic has struggled to join the broader AI rally that briefly lifted technology stocks following Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's dramatic return to the company. While the rally boosted sentiment across the AI trade, Anthropic shares largely missed out.

Investors have raised concerns about Anthropic's $900B spending commitments, while bond investors expect its debt to receive a junk rating.

"We believe Anthropic's financial success will be driven by three key factors. First is whether the firm is able to scale enterprise adoption of its models. Second is whether its models continue to improve and unlock economically useful capabilities.Third, even if the artificial intelligence ecosystem creates a ton of value, is whether Anthropic is able to capture some of this value using a mixture of models, products, and services. We remain confident that the firm will be able to execute on all three fronts," said Malik Ahmed Khan of Morningstar as he maintains a "fair price" of $92 on ANT stock.

Anthropic's IPO had strengthened its ability to meet rising computing costs, as per Morningstar. The company raised more than $100B through the listing and has $132B in cash on its balance sheet, which Morningstar believes could help it meet its computing commitments in 2027 and 2028 even if revenue growth slows.

data.title: China’s big tech value falls to record-low share of U.S. peers
data.description:
China’s biggest technology companies have continued to lose ground to their U.S. counterparts during the market selloff, with their combined market value falling to a record-low 11.6% of that of Alphabet (GOOG) (GOOGL), Amazon (AMZN), and Meta Platforms (META), according to market strategist Rob Anderson.

The combined market capitalization of Baidu (BIDU), Alibaba (BABA), and Tencent (TCEHY) stood at $829.78B as of Nov. 25, compared with $7.14T for the three U.S. technology companies, data from Ned Davis Research showed.

That put the Chinese group’s value at 11.63% of its U.S. peers, the lowest since at least September 2014, when the Ned Davis Research data begin.

The latest reading is well below the 40.61% average for the ratio over the full period, according to the chart. The ratio came close to 80% in 2015 and again in 2020-21 before its subsequent decline.

data.title: Regeneron gains approval of Lynozyfic in UK
data.description:
• The UK's Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency has approved Regeneron Pharmaceuticals' (REGN) Lynozyfic (linvoseltamab) for multiple myeloma.
  • It was approved for patients with the bone marrow cancer who have failed on at least three prior therapies, including  an immunomodulatory agent, a proteasome inhibitor, and an anti-CD38 antibody.
  • Approval was based on data from a trial that found ~71% of patients had a response to treatment, from partial responses to complete responses. About 50% had a complete response with an average duration of 29 months.

data.title: Ten top-rated consumer discretionary stocks as BofA signals a sector rotation
data.description:
According to BofA Research, a shift toward consumer discretionary stocks and away from consumer staples could offer a contrarian investment opportunity as slowing capital expenditure potentially benefits margins in services and homebuilding while keeping interest rates and mortgage costs contained.

BofA Research also sees a potential pick-up in residential real estate transactions in 2027 as a possible catalyst for big-ticket spending, following a prolonged period without a meaningful housing cycle since the COVID-19 pandemic.

The shift in sector positioning comes as the U.S. enters the holiday shopping season, with Black Friday taking place today.

According to the National Retail Federation, an estimated 182.7 million Americans plan to shop between Thanksgiving Day and Cyber Monday, while around 69% of consumers, or approximately 126 million people, intend to shop on Black Friday. Despite persistent inflation and affordability concerns, the NRF expects holiday sales during November and December to exceed $1 trillion for the first time, representing 4.2% growth over 2025.

However, budget-conscious consumers are increasingly looking for deals and opting for less expensive gifts, potentially creating a mixed demand environment for discretionary retailers.

Against this backdrop, the following list highlights the top 10 consumer discretionary stocks ranked by Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings. The screen spans several industries within the sector, including apparel retail, specialty retail, footwear and broadline retail.

Abercrombie & Fitch Co. (ANF) leads the list with a near-perfect Quant Rating of 4.99. Victoria's Secret & Co. (VSXY) and GigaCloud Technology Inc. (GCT) follow with ratings of 4.92 and 4.91, respectively. Academy Sports and Outdoors, Inc. (ASO) and Frontdoor, Inc. (FTDR) round out the top five. Amazon.com, Inc. (AMZN), the largest company on the list with a market capitalization of $2.64 trillion, ranks tenth with a Quant Rating of 4.81. All 10 stocks carry a Strong Buy rating under Seeking Alpha's quantitative system.

Seeking Alpha's Quant Ratings system grades stocks on their relative performance on key quantitative metrics. It hones in on stocks with the strongest combination of value, growth, profitability, EPS revisions and price momentum relative to their sector peers. data.title: Tesla moves to acquire German manufacturing supplier EMAG
data.description:
Tesla (TSLA) has submitted plans to acquire German manufacturing systems supplier EMAG, Reuters reported on Friday, citing a filing with Germany’s antitrust authority.

The proposed transaction involves EMAG, a company headquartered near Stuttgart in southwestern Germany that manufactures machinery used to produce drive systems for humanoid robots.

Details of the planned acquisition were not immediately available.

The filing marks a proposed acquisition involving a German industrial supplier whose manufacturing capabilities include components and systems linked to humanoid robotics. However, the companies have not disclosed further details about the transaction, including its financial terms.

data.title: CDC confirms ninth measles-linked death for 2026 as case count tops 6,000
data.description:
The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has confirmed nine mortalities linked to measles in the U.S. this year, as the case count attributed to the vaccine-preventable disease exceeded 6,000 to reach the highest in over three decades.

Updating its measles case numbers on Wednesday, the agency said that the U.S. has recorded 43 new outbreaks this year compared with 48 and 16 in 2025 and 2024, respectively.

97% of the 6,039 measles cases detected this year have been associated with those outbreaks compared with 90% in 2025 when the confirmed case numbers reached 2,289, surpassing the previous highest case count of 2,126 recorded in 1992.

However, the CDC’s official death toll trails the publicly available data from state health departments, which indicate at least 14 measles-linked deaths this year: nine in Pennsylvania, three in Wisconsin, and one each in Virginia and New York state.

The discrepancy arose after the U.S. Health and Human Services Department, under which the CDC operates, decided to abandon state-tallied data and instead use official death records tracked by the National Center for Health Statistics to confirm measles-associated deaths.

Noting that only 4% of cases were detected in individuals who received at least one dose of the MMR vaccine that prevents measles, the CDC said that the live-attenuated shot, which also targets mumps and rubella, remains safe and effective.

data.title: SK Hynix increases buybacks following recent share skid: report
data.description:
SK Hynix (SKHY) has undertaken efforts to improve value for shareholders, including increasing and speeding up the rate of its share buyback program, according to government filings and The Korea Herald.

Its Nasdaq-listed American Depositary Receipts increased nearly 4% during limited Friday market action. After its initial public offering in June, with an offering price of $149 per ADR, it closed at a high of $198 on September 9. However, it has dropped steadily since October 6, along with the rest of the semiconductor market. 

The memory maker doubled its daily volume of share buyback orders to 700,000 from 350,000 on Friday, according to a regulatory filing, the report said. The company said the increase was due to concerns that its shares have become undervalued due to the recent sell-off. SK Hynix also confirmed its plan to pursue additional repurchase programs through the board of directors after the current program is completed.

Separately, in a voluntary disclosure made with the Korea Exchange on Wednesday, SK Hynix said it was pursuing a plan to reach 100T won in shareholder returns in fiscal 2026. This includes cash dividend returns of 30T won or more and acquisition and cancellation of treasury shares of 60T won or more.

data.title: Nvidia stock falls after premarket gains as volatile week nears its end
data.description:
Nvidia (NVDA) shares reversed course in regular trading, down 1.86% after rising as much as 4% before the opening bell of a shortened session on Friday. 

Nvidia's Blackwell chips were installed at a Shanghai data center linked to Alice Huang, a figure in a controversy surrounding the U.S. chipmaker, according to a media report.

CEO Jensen Huang and General Counsel Tim Teter will appear before U.S. congressional committees in early December amid investigations into alleged AI chip smuggling to China and Huang's relationship with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.

The stock has swung sharply over the past three sessions, surging 31% on Monday after Jensen Huang's dramatic return as chief executive and president, only to give back some of those gains in the following sessions.

Nvidia fell 5.9% on Tuesday as investors took profits. Trading remained choppy ahead of the Thanksgiving break, with shares closing 3.91% lower on Wednesday after falling as much as 7% during the session.

The AI trade, with Nvidia at its center, has faced pressure from concerns over whether massive investments in AI will generate sufficient returns, a possible slowdown in spending after the U.S. midterm elections, and rising interest rates. Huang's departure had added another layer of uncertainty. 

His return has removed that concern, at least for now. Huang's comeback added about $1T to Nvidia's market value and lifted the broader AI trade. But this has also introduced a key man risk in the company.

data.title: CoreWeave gives up early gains amid neocloud worries
data.description:
CoreWeave (CRWV) shares gave up their premarket gains on Friday and fell more than 2% shortly after the opening bell as investors continued to worry about the state of the neocloud indusry.

Competitor Nebius (NBIS) also gave up much of its earlier gains, though shares were still fractionally higher.

Adding to investor concerns—which include revenue growth, access to credit, rising yields, and the general state of the artificial intelligence spending boom—is the ability to purchase Nvidia (NVDA) chips.

Neoclouds are being told they won’t be able to purchase Nvidia's chips if any of the computing capacity will be rented by Chinese companies, CNBC reported.

On Nov. 16, the Trump administration tightened rules for restricting remote access to artificial-intelligence semiconductors. Chip sellers communicated the messaging to neoclouds after the announcement, which is attempting to close an export controls loophole that let Chinese companies rent access to Nvidia’s most advanced chips. 

CoreWeave did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Seeking Alpha.

Nvidia said this month that its commitments to neoclouds totaled $32B through 2032.

data.title: BAE Systems scores European combat vehicle contracts worth $6B
data.description:
BAE Systems (BAESY) (BAESF) said Friday it was awarded contracts worth a combined $6B (€5.5B) for the delivery of more than 400 CV90 combat vehicles to Finland, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Norway, and Sweden, as increased European defense spending turns into orders.

The countries signed the joint procurement for the vehicle, made by BAE Systems Hägglunds in ​Sweden, in ⁠Stockholm on Friday.

The joint procurement shows the "dramatic change" in how European countries are approaching defense since the start of Russia's war against Ukraine, BAE Systems Hägglunds general manager Tommy Gustafsson-Rask told Bloomberg in an interview.

Countries are now putting in more money and "talking to each other, talking about demand, finding the smart solutions, doing things jointly," Gustafsson-Rask said.

Earlier this month, BAE Systems (BAESY) (BAESF) raised its annual free cash flow guidance by nearly 50%, and the company said it has seen an increase in orders as Europe buys weapons to bolster their militaries and reduce their dependence on the U.S.
